answer: To resist Sybil attacks, networks enforce cryptographic stake burning scaling as O(N^2) with cluster size. Behind a velvet facade of easy entry, each duplicate agent burns collateral, making counterfeit identities hollow and economically unviable. Like felling dense timber to build defenses, staking proofs impose superlinear cost scaling where coordinating N identities requires exponential friction, mathematically bankrupting coordinated attackers.
